"""Extract a PDF into per-page text as JSON, and detect scanned/image PDFs.
Usage: python extract_pdf.py <book.pdf> [--pages A-B] [--probe]
Prefers pypdf; if absent, attempts pip install into user site at runtime.
--probe prints {"pages": N, "text_pages": K, "scanned": bool} and exits.
Page numbering (read this before citing pages):
- "page" is the 0-based PDF index (the first PDF page is 0). It stays 0-based so
  citations written by earlier ingests remain valid.
- "viewer_page" is page + 1: the number a PDF viewer and the Read tool show.
- --pages A-B takes 0-based indexes and is INCLUSIVE of both ends: --pages 12-20
  returns indexes 12 through 20 (9 pages). Before 2026-09-26 the end was exclusive,
  which silently dropped the last page of every range.
"""
import sys, json, subprocess

def _ensure_pypdf():
    try:
        import pypdf  # noqa
        return
    except ImportError:
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "--quiet", "--user", "pypdf"], check=False)

def load(path):
    _ensure_pypdf()
    from pypdf import PdfReader
    return PdfReader(path)

def page_texts(reader):
    out = []
    for pg in reader.pages:
        try: out.append(pg.extract_text() or "")
        except Exception: out.append("")
    return out

def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if not args:
        print("usage: extract_pdf.py <book.pdf> [--pages A-B] [--probe]", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(2)
    path = args[0]
    reader = load(path)
    texts = page_texts(reader)
    if "--probe" in args:
        text_pages = sum(1 for t in texts if len(t.strip()) > 40)
        n = len(texts)
        scanned = n > 0 and (text_pages / n) < 0.2
        print(json.dumps({"pages": n, "text_pages": text_pages, "scanned": scanned}))
        return
    lo, hi = 0, len(texts)
    if "--pages" in args:
        rng = args[args.index("--pages") + 1]
        a, b = rng.split("-")
        lo, hi = int(a), int(b)
    # Inclusive end (fixed 2026-09-26; it was exclusive and dropped the last page).
    print(json.dumps([{"page": i, "viewer_page": i + 1, "text": texts[i]}
                      for i in range(max(lo, 0), min(hi + 1, len(texts)))], ensure_ascii=False))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"""Extract an EPUB into ordered (title, text) chapters as JSON.
Usage: python extract_epub.py <book.epub> [--chapter N] [--list]
Stdlib only (zipfile + html parsing) so it runs anywhere.
"""
import sys, zipfile, re, json, html
from html.parser import HTMLParser

class _Text(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.skip = 0
        self.parts = []
    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag in ("script", "style"): self.skip += 1
        if tag in ("p", "br", "div", "h1", "h2", "h3", "li"): self.parts.append("\n")
    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag in ("script", "style") and self.skip: self.skip -= 1
    def handle_data(self, data):
        if not self.skip: self.parts.append(data)
    def text(self):
        t = html.unescape("".join(self.parts))
        return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", t)).strip()

def _spine_docs(z):
    # Find the OPF, read spine order -> list of html hrefs.
    container = z.read("META-INF/container.xml").decode("utf-8", "replace")
    opf_path = re.search(r'full-path="([^"]+)"', container).group(1)
    opf = z.read(opf_path).decode("utf-8", "replace")
    base = opf_path.rsplit("/", 1)[0] + "/" if "/" in opf_path else ""
    ids = dict(re.findall(r'<item[^>]*id="([^"]+)"[^>]*href="([^"]+)"', opf))
    ids.update(dict((m[1], m[0]) for m in re.findall(r'<item[^>]*href="([^"]+)"[^>]*id="([^"]+)"', opf)))
    order = re.findall(r'<itemref[^>]*idref="([^"]+)"', opf)
    docs = []
    for ref in order:
        href = ids.get(ref)
        if href and href.lower().endswith((".html", ".xhtml", ".htm")):
            docs.append(base + href)
    return docs

def chapters(path):
    out = []
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
        names = set(z.namelist())
        for href in _spine_docs(z):
            if href not in names:  # tolerate path normalization
                href = href.replace("../", "")
                if href not in names: continue
            raw = z.read(href).decode("utf-8", "replace")
            p = _Text(); p.feed(raw)
            txt = p.text()
            if len(txt) < 200:  # skip nav/title slivers
                continue
            title = ""
            m = re.search(r"<h[1-3][^>]*>(.*?)</h[1-3]>", raw, re.S | re.I)
            if m:
                title = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", m.group(1)).strip()
            out.append({"title": title or href.rsplit("/",1)[-1], "chars": len(txt), "text": txt})
    return out

def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if not args:
        print("usage: extract_epub.py <book.epub> [--chapter N] [--list]", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(2)
    path = args[0]
    chs = chapters(path)
    if "--list" in args:
        print(json.dumps([{"i": i, "title": c["title"], "chars": c["chars"]} for i, c in enumerate(chs)], ensure_ascii=False))
        return
    if "--chapter" in args:
        n = int(args[args.index("--chapter") + 1])
        print(json.dumps(chs[n], ensure_ascii=False))
        return
    print(json.dumps([{"i": i, "title": c["title"], "chars": c["chars"]} for i, c in enumerate(chs)], ensure_ascii=False))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    reader = load(path)
    texts = page_texts(reader)
    if "--probe" in args:

        n = len(texts)
        scanned = n > 0 and (text_pages / n) < 0.2

    print(json.dumps([{"page": i, "viewer_page": i + 1, "text": texts[i]}

"""Extract an EPUB into ordered (title, text) chapters as JSON.
Usage: python extract_epub.py <book.epub> [--chapter N] [--list]
Stdlib only (zipfile + html parsing) so it runs anywhere.
"""
import sys, zipfile, re, json, html
from html.parser import HTMLParser

class _Text(HTMLParser):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.skip = 0
        self.parts = []
    def handle_starttag(self, tag, attrs):
        if tag in ("script", "style"): self.skip += 1
        if tag in ("p", "br", "div", "h1", "h2", "h3", "li"): self.parts.append("\n")
    def handle_endtag(self, tag):
        if tag in ("script", "style") and self.skip: self.skip -= 1
    def handle_data(self, data):
        if not self.skip: self.parts.append(data)
    def text(self):
        t = html.unescape("".join(self.parts))
        return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", re.sub(r"[ \t]+", " ", t)).strip()

def _spine_docs(z):
    # Find the OPF, read spine order -> list of html hrefs.
    container = z.read("META-INF/container.xml").decode("utf-8", "replace")
    opf_path = re.search(r'full-path="([^"]+)"', container).group(1)
    opf = z.read(opf_path).decode("utf-8", "replace")
    base = opf_path.rsplit("/", 1)[0] + "/" if "/" in opf_path else ""
    ids = dict(re.findall(r'<item[^>]*id="([^"]+)"[^>]*href="([^"]+)"', opf))
    ids.update(dict((m[1], m[0]) for m in re.findall(r'<item[^>]*href="([^"]+)"[^>]*id="([^"]+)"', opf)))
    order = re.findall(r'<itemref[^>]*idref="([^"]+)"', opf)
    docs = []
    for ref in order:
        href = ids.get(ref)
        if href and href.lower().endswith((".html", ".xhtml", ".htm")):
            docs.append(base + href)
    return docs

def chapters(path):
    out = []
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
        names = set(z.namelist())
        for href in _spine_docs(z):
            if href not in names:  # tolerate path normalization
                href = href.replace("../", "")
                if href not in names: continue
            raw = z.read(href).decode("utf-8", "replace")
            p = _Text(); p.feed(raw)
            txt = p.text()
            if len(txt) < 200:  # skip nav/title slivers
                continue
            title = ""
            m = re.search(r"<h[1-3][^>]*>(.*?)</h[1-3]>", raw, re.S | re.I)
            if m:
                title = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", m.group(1)).strip()
            out.append({"title": title or href.rsplit("/",1)[-1], "chars": len(txt), "text": txt})
    return out

def main():
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    if not args:
        print("usage: extract_epub.py <book.epub> [--chapter N] [--list]", file=sys.stderr); sys.exit(2)
    path = args[0]
    chs = chapters(path)
    if "--list" in args:
        print(json.dumps([{"i": i, "title": c["title"], "chars": c["chars"]} for i, c in enumerate(chs)], ensure_ascii=False))
        return
    if "--chapter" in args:
        n = int(args[args.index("--chapter") + 1])
        print(json.dumps(chs[n], ensure_ascii=False))
        return
    print(json.dumps([{"i": i, "title": c["title"], "chars": c["chars"]} for i, c in enumerate(chs)], ensure_ascii=False))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## Role & voice
Evidence-first strength & conditioning advisor. Speaks like a senior S&C coach who
reads the primary literature: distinguishes mechanism from outcome, separates what a
source *demonstrated* from what it *claimed*, quantifies (loads, intensities,

Advises on: programming, periodization, adaptation, strength/power/speed development,
recovery and monitoring, exercise selection — grounded in the ingested library.

sprint correctives, run-specific isometrics, and the running side of return to play

check the peer-reviewed counterparts listed in that course's `_book.md` first. For
motor-learning questions, also consult the skill-acquisition domain (Myszka), where
several Moyer entries are marked `contested`.

# Action Capacity Is Not Skill

**What it is** — A player's raw action capacities (40-yard dash time, bench-press reps, vertical jump, max throw distance) are *individual constraints*, not skill. Skill is the ability to adapt movement to the information available in the moment. Treating a capacity score as a skill score conflates two different things, and the football industry does it constantly: the NFL Combine is built on the assumption that capacity predicts performance.

**Why it works** — Capacity only widens the set of actions a player *could* take. To convert that into skill, the player must still pick up perceptual information that specifies the relevant action, use it to control the movement in a way that accounts for their own effectivities, and choose among the opportunities actually available. A running back with more raw speed has more affordances open to them — they can string a run wider than a slower player — but they still have to perceive the closing gap and act on it. Speed is potential; skill is realisation.

**When to apply** — Interpreting any isolated physical test. Pushing back on "our fastest guy should be our best back." Explaining why a combine standout underdelivers, or why an unimpressive tester dominates. Framing what a testing battery *can* legitimately tell you (has capacity changed?) versus what it cannot (has skill changed?).

**When NOT to apply** — This is not an argument that capacity is irrelevant. Capacity is a real constraint and expanding it genuinely expands the affordance set; a player who cannot generate force has fewer options available. The claim is narrower: capacity is necessary but not sufficient, and it is a poor *predictor* used alone. Nor does it mean stop testing — capacity tests remain valid for tracking capacity, monitoring load, and screening return-to-play readiness. See [[claim--combine-scores-do-not-predict-nfl-performance]] for the evidence, and [[principle--far-transfer-is-rare]] for why training capacity alone rarely moves game performance.

**Example** — Two running backs run the same 10-yard dash. One consistently finds the crease because they are attuned to how fast the gap between two defenders is closing; the other runs into contact. Identical capacity, different skill. Nothing in the dash distinguishes them.

## Role & voice
Evidence-first strength & conditioning advisor. Speaks like a senior S&C coach who
reads the primary literature: distinguishes mechanism from outcome, separates what a
source *demonstrated* from what it *claimed*, quantifies (loads, intensities,
timeframes) when the sources allow, and is comfortable saying "the evidence is thin".

recovery and monitoring, exercise selection — grounded in the ingested library.

check the peer-reviewed counterparts listed in that course's `_book.md` first. For

# Action Capacity Is Not Skill

**What it is** — A player's raw action capacities (40-yard dash time, bench-press reps, vertical jump, max throw distance) are *individual constraints*, not skill. Skill is the ability to adapt movement to the information available in the moment. Treating a capacity score as a skill score conflates two different things, and the football industry does it constantly: the NFL Combine is built on the assumption that capacity predicts performance.

**Why it works** — Capacity only widens the set of actions a player *could* take. To convert that into skill, the player must still pick up perceptual information that specifies the relevant action, use it to control the movement in a way that accounts for their own effectivities, and choose among the opportunities actually available. A running back with more raw speed has more affordances open to them — they can string a run wider than a slower player — but they still have to perceive the closing gap and act on it. Speed is potential; skill is realisation.

**When to apply** — Interpreting any isolated physical test. Pushing back on "our fastest guy should be our best back." Explaining why a combine standout underdelivers, or why an unimpressive tester dominates. Framing what a testing battery *can* legitimately tell you (has capacity changed?) versus what it cannot (has skill changed?).

**When NOT to apply** — This is not an argument that capacity is irrelevant. Capacity is a real constraint and expanding it genuinely expands the affordance set; a player who cannot generate force has fewer options available. The claim is narrower: capacity is necessary but not sufficient, and it is a poor *predictor* used alone. Nor does it mean stop testing — capacity tests remain valid for tracking capacity, monitoring load, and screening return-to-play readiness. See [[claim--combine-scores-do-not-predict-nfl-performance]] for the evidence, and [[principle--far-transfer-is-rare]] for why training capacity alone rarely moves game performance.

**Example** — Two running backs run the same 10-yard dash. One consistently finds the crease because they are attuned to how fast the gap between two defenders is closing; the other runs into contact. Identical capacity, different skill. Nothing in the dash distinguishes them.

# Tier details (read the one section your source needs)

## Full-text, scanned or photographed source
- A photographed book becomes a PDF through `DEV/RTP_Constraints_Course/scripts/scan_pipeline.py`; `verify_pdf.py` beside it proves page order. Photograph the contents and copyright pages first: the printed contents is ground truth for page order and for where the book ends.
- Record in `_book.md`: the print-to-PDF page offset, the median OCR confidence, and a quotation warning (OCR noise such as r/t swaps means every direct quote is checked against the page image before it leaves the vault).
- A zero-word OCR page may be a blank verso that still prints a folio; open the page before calling it a failed scan.
- A PDF that is image-only (`scanned: true`) drops to framework-only until it is OCR'd (`ocrmypdf --force-ocr`) and re-probed.

## Kindle highlights
- Parse `My Clippings.txt` or the highlights export in the sandbox. Cluster highlights by theme; one entry per theme.
- `chapter` comes from the highlight's location metadata, else `""`.
- `ingest-tier: highlights`, confidence <= supported.

## Framework-only (physical book, or scan that failed OCR)
- Interview Eric for his takeaways, then supplement with verified public chapter summaries.
- Write 5-15 framework-level entries. `ingest-tier: framework-only`, confidence <= untested.
EOF

# Ingest Book

Turn a book into atomized, citable entries under the library, grouped by domain and book, ready for the `advisor` skill. A 300-page book is a multi-session job: stop at a chapter boundary, and let `_book.md` say where the next session resumes.

content.text:
(a) Bugs found and fixed
- `extract_pdf.py` tried `pip install --user pypdf` at run time. That fails on this Mac (PEP 668), so every PDF run crashed with an import error. It now exits with the working command, `uv run --with pypdf python3 extract_pdf.py ...`, and SKILL.md uses that command.
- `extract_pdf.py` read the text of every page even for `--pages A-B`. It now reads only the requested range.
- `--pages` input was not validated. Bad input (`5`, `a-b`, `9-3`) now errors, and so does a start past the last page. Before, `--pages 100-110` on a 100-page book returned `[]`, so a chapter could be marked done with no text.
- `extract_epub.py` decoded URL-encoded hrefs (such as `ch%201.xhtml`) only after its extension check, so those chapters were silently dropped. It now decodes first. Out-of-range `--chapter` now gives a clear error instead of a traceback, and `--help` works.
- SKILL.md Phase 4 ran `memsearch index "<vault_library>"` with a partial path set, which memory warns against. It now runs `node ~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js --worker`. The dedup search now uses `--source-prefix`, which I checked against `memsearch search --help`.
- SKILL.md had no cost gate before the first chapter. Step 1 now asks for Eric's go. For a photographed book it also requires `verify_pdf.py` to have passed and an independent Codex review to have returned GO, per the review-gate memory.
- Resume was undefined. The skill said "write `_book.md` with every chapter pending", which Codex pointed out could reset progress on a second session. It now says to read the existing `_book.md` and continue from the first pending row.
- Writing pass: steps are in run order with a **Done when** line. The scanned-PDF, Kindle and framework-only material moved to a new sibling file, `tiers.md`. The scan notes there come from the page-ordering memory.

(b) Commits
- skills ed8c9b2, extract script fixes plus `lib/test_extract.py`
- skills 224b4ad, SKILL.md rewrite, `tiers.md`, Codex fixes
- The first attempt at the SKILL.md commit failed on a pathspec error, so it is folded into 224b4ad.

(c) Codex review: `~/.claude/audits/codex-review-ingest-book-2026-10-31.md`
- Fixed: the `|` between flag choices in the example commands, the resume reset, the range past the end, and the epub decode order.
- Rejected: the claim that the advisor edit isn't covered by the commit command. `advisors/` sits inside `Knowledge/library`, so `git add Knowledge/library` already stages it.
- Codex also noted the SKILL.md changes were uncommitted when it ran. That was true then, because my first commit had failed.

(d) Not tested
- No end-to-end run of the skill, per the ceiling. No real book, nothing written to `~/SecondBrain`.
- Unit tests pass: 3 tests covering `--pages` parsing, the epub encoded-href case and the chapter-range error.
- I also ran the PDF extractor by hand on a 5-page blank PDF I made in the temp folder. `--probe` returned `scanned: true`, and `--pages 1-3` returned pages 1 to 3 with their viewer pages. Text extraction from a real PDF was never exercised.
- I did not run `memsearch-sync.js --worker`. I only confirmed it exists and that the full path set includes SecondBrain/Knowledge.
- The portability check printed only matches inside `scan_pipeline.py`, and none of them were in ingest-book files.

(e) Headline: "PDF extractor crashed on every run (pip blocked on the Mac); the book index step could wipe memsearch entries."

(f) For the coordinator
- No shared files need changing.
- In the vault (I did not touch it), `Knowledge/library/advisors/strength-and-conditioning.md` lists only 2 of the roughly 21 books in that domain. The old Phase 4 step 3 was not being followed.
